content:
tim-sales: POC kickoff Fri for SierraMed. They want Redwood Private running in their AWS account. Main asks: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering, single static egress IP, and whether we can avoid SNAT so their downstream IDS sees original client IPs.

maya-se: Quick clarifier: theyplan to deploy our package into their EKS cluster, right? Or are they asking for a provider-hosted endpoint we connect to?

tim-sales: They'll run it in their account (customer-hosted). They want the runtime to call back to our control plane for licensing/metrics. Also need a short network preflight for netops and a line-itemed list of infra costs.

raj-netops: Network notes:
- VPC Peering: L3 routing, no transitive routes, requires unique CIDRs. Good if they need broad access among VPCs.
- AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint): service-level connection via ENIs in consumer subnets. Does not expose full routing; recommended if they only want specific service ports.
- Single static egress IP: use NAT Gateway with EIP or put traffic through their central egress proxy. NAT will SNAT; original client IP will be lost unless app/proxy inserts X-Forwarded-For.
- To preserve original IP without SNAT: you need routing that avoids NAT (e.g., direct routing to on-prem via Transit Gateway or a proxy that forwards metadata). Native TCP preserves IP only if not NATed.

emily-security: Security checklist items to include in the questionnaire:
- Outbound HTTPS (443) to our control plane FQDNs (we'll provide names). Avoid IP-based firewalling when possible.
- ECR/registry access for image pulls (443). If they block internet egress, provide S3/ECR VPC endpoints or a cached repo.
- VPC Flow Logs enabled and retention policy stated.
- If they require mTLS for control plane, we support it but need cert exchange details.

alex.solutions: Cost bullets to send customer:
- Redwood Private license/platform fee (our billing).
- Customer infra: EC2/GPU or EKS node costs, NAT Gateway hours + EIP, NLB if used, PrivateLink ENI & data processing fees.
- Suggest budgeting for cross-AZ ENIs if using PrivateLink (one ENI per AZ).

tim-sales: They also asked: if we suggest PrivateLink, do we need them to create endpoint subnets and SG rules? Any sample SG rules we can give them quickly?

raj-netops: Yes. Minimal guidance for PrivateLink consumer side:
- Create interface endpoint in at least two AZs.
- Subnet security group: allow outbound to service ports (443) and inbound from the endpoint ENI SG for the service ports.
- If using internal ALB/NLB for our services, ensure SGs allow the necessary health-check ports.

emily-security: Add to checklist: require that the endpoint subnets are private (no internet route) and restrict admin CIDRs for SSH/console-only access. Also request their audit role for verifying flow logs once POC is live.

deploy-bot: doc: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/private-deploy/network-checklist

tim-sales: OK can we turn this into a one-page preflight and a two-line firewall snippet to paste to their netops team? I'll join their call Thu 9am PT to run through.

maya-se: Ill draft the one-pager and firewall snippet and post it here by EOD.

raj-netops: I'll join Thu call for the handoff.

emily-security: I'll join first 30 mins to cover questionnaire answers.

tim-sales: Thanks all :thumbsup:
